fields.why: Every computed contrast is a ratio or percent change ("8% higher", "2.9 times higher", "2.4 times as high"); no percentage-point difference is reported. B's only support for absolute is the t-test significance mark, which is inference, not a reported scale.

brief_issues: Unclear whether a test of a difference (pairwise t-test on percentages) with no reported difference makes the scale absolute; a rule saying scale follows the reported contrast, not the test, would settle it. B also left data_focus ev empty and cited a URL as data-source evidence.
